cues.text: A routing table records the destination prefix, next hop or interface, preference and metric.
Connected routes appear when the configured interfaces are operational.
A static route is set manually; it is simple and predictable, but won't normally adapt to failures without tracking or automation.
Dynamic routing protocols exchange reachability and converge as topology changes.
The IPv4 default route, zero dot zero dot zero dot zero slash zero, catches destinations with no more specific route.
Its metric is hop count, fifteen usable hops maximum, sixteen unreachable.
It uses periodic updates and loop mitigation, making it useful for simple teaching networks.
Routers establish adjacencies, flood link-state advertisements, build a link-state database, then run Dijkstra's shortest-path-first algorithm using cost.
Areas limit flooding and organise a hierarchy.
BGP is inter-domain path-vector routing, driven by policy, autonomous-system path and other attributes, not simply geographic distance.
Interior gateway protocols operate within an autonomous system; BGP commonly exchanges routes between autonomous systems.
